newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Santander Q1 net up 24 pct, Latam shines.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Santander Q1 net up 24 pct, Latam shines.

text.p: Spain's Banco Santander posted a 23.7 percent rise in first-quarter earnings on Tuesday, underpinned by a robust core performance and a strong contribution from Latin American business.

Spain's biggest bank said net attributable profit rose to 24.8 billion pesetas ($170.1 million) in the three months to March from 20.05 billion in the year-earlier period, with earnings outstripping financial analysts' consensus expectations of a 21 percent gain.
Supporting the results were a 22.5 percent rise in net interest income, a 27 percent increase in ordinary margin and a 46 percent gain in operating income.
"These are better than expected, with a strong performance at the operating level," a dealer at Central Hispano Bolsa brokerage said.
The core performance was "helped by strong growth in fee and commission income from services and financial operations," Santander said in a statement.
"Growth at the bank is focused on value-added services," executive vice-president Francisco Luzon told reporters.
Over a third of earnings were contributed by the group's Latin American businesses after the recent completion of purchases of Banco de Venezuela, Chile's Banco Osorno y La Union and BCH Puerto Rico.
Latin American holdings contributed 9.75 billion pesetas to net attributable income, the bank said.
At the end of the period, purchases of Banco Mexicano, Banco Comercial Antioqueno and Banco Geral do Comercio in Brazil had not been completed.
On the whole, retail banking accounted for 75.7 percent of group attributable income, up from 68.9 percent this time last year.

"The increased contribution of retail banking to net attributable income in large part reflects strong activity in the subsidiaries abroad, especially in Latin America and Europe where all group banks are profitable," the bank said.
The bank improved its non performing loans ratio to 3.10 percent versus 4.01 percent a year ago after "strict credit risk management."
Santander also confirmed that it would split its shares three for one on June 9, reducing the face value to 250 pesetas from 750 pesetas.
Shares in the bank rose after the results announcement, gaining four percent to 10,720 pesetas.
